Test image observations: Green mango leaf with irregular brown/dark necrotic lesions concentrated along the leaf margin and scattered on the blade. Lesions have somewhat defined edges, some with lighter centers. No white powder, no sooty coating. Damage pattern suggests a fungal disease affecting leaf tissue.

Top candidates: Anthracnose (irregular brown spots/lesions on leaves) and Die_Back (necrosis). Let me check one reference per class first.
Anthracnose ref 1: Nearly fully yellowed/browned leaf - quite different from test image's green leaf with discrete lesions.
Die_Back ref 1: Completely desiccated brown/dead leaf - not matching.
Powdery_Mildew ref 1: Shows whitish/powdery coating across leaf surface - not matching test image's brown necrotic lesions.

Sooty_Mould ref 1: Dark black speckling across green leaf - not matching.

Test image best matches Anthracnose so far (brown irregular necrotic lesions). Let me view more Anthracnose references.
Anthracnose ref 2: Green leaf with irregular dark brown/black necrotic lesions — very close match to the test image pattern.

Anthracnose ref 3: Green leaf with discrete dark brown necrotic spots — matches the test image well.

One more view remaining. Let me check Die_Back ref 2 to rule it out fully.

Die_Back ref 2: Completely dried, brown, shriveled leaf — nothing like the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: green mango leaf with irregular brown/dark necrotic lesions along margin and blade
- Anthracnose refs 2 & 3: green leaves with discrete dark brown lesions — strong visual match
- Die_Back: fully desiccated brown leaves — no match
- Powdery_Mildew: white powdery coating — no match
- Sooty_Mould: black speckling — no match
